verdicts.why: Names an exchange on a topic without rating it; plain neighbour of talk or conversation.
Describes free, stream-like movement of ideas or wit; the ease is the meaning, not an attitude beyond it.
Plain physical motion of a liquid; no side taken.
Hair or cloth falling in a certain way is described, not judged.
Abundance is the meaning of the sense; the word does not approve or disapprove of what is abundant.
Causative of plain motion; descriptive only.
Covering with water is a bare physical event; no attitude carried.
A dated euphemism for menstruate: choosing it signals delicacy or avoidance rather than approval or contempt, and I cannot settle whether that counts as judging the referent.
Names a sense faculty; nothing to judge.
A legal proceeding named in plain terms; no side taken.
An opportunity to be heard is described neutrally; any fairness judgement comes from the modifier, not the noun.
Range of audibility is a plain spatial notion.
The act of listening attentively is described, not rated.
A committee session named in institutional plain language.
Names a kind of lodging; older-fashioned than hotel but not evaluative of the place.
Not wide is a bare dimension, as in the narrowest part of the water.
Limited in scope, as in the narrow sense of a word or narrow space, is descriptive; the disapproving narrow-minded sense is a different synset.
A narrow margin or escape states degree only; no attitude beyond the meaning.
The activity of reading is named without praise or blame; any approval in the sentences belongs to the speakers.
An interpretation or performance is named neutrally.
Written material to be read; plain referent, plain word.
A meter datum is technical and attitude-free.
A mental construal of meaning is described, not judged.
A public recitation is named as an event type only.
The act of taking a measurement carries no attitude.
Being reconciled to something reports the subject's acceptance; the unwelcomeness of the thing is part of the meaning, not a speaker judgement.
Making one thing compatible with another is a plain operation.
Coming to terms is described without rating either party.
Bringing into accord is neutral; the plain neighbour of harmonise.
Names a caused outcome with no attitude toward it.
